q: Does oxy-fuel firing lower a furnace's carbon footprint?
title: Oxy-fuel firing: footprint effect
short: It cuts fuel, because burners no longer heat the nitrogen in air. But making oxygen takes electricity. Your Scope 1 falls; your Scope 2 rises if you run an oxygen plant, or Scope 3 rises if you buy liquid oxygen. Count both before calling it a saving.
audience: Glass, metal melting and frit furnace operators

ul: Oxygen plant electricity is added (Scope 2), or bought oxygen (Scope 3, Category 1).
Flue gas volume drops, which helps any heat recovery or capture later.

ol: Fuel saved per tonne multiplied by its factor.
Minus oxygen used per tonne multiplied by the electricity per tonne of oxygen and 0.710 kg CO2 per kWh for FY 2024-25, or the supplier's figure for bought oxygen.
The difference is the net change.

senseible: Senseible reads fuel invoices and electricity bills and applies IPCC 2006 factors and the CEA grid factor (0.710 kg CO2 per kWh for FY 2024-25), so you can compare Scope 1 and 2 before and after a change from the documents themselves.
